The data show a clear association between plcg and pakts473 (correlation 0.44), so C is unlikely. I picked the direction from prior knowledge of this signalling network, not from anything in the data. I did not run any causal-direction test, so the choice of A over B is a judgement call.

This dataset matches the well-known Sachs et al. flow-cytometry signalling data. In that network, plcg sits upstream: it acts through PIP2 and PKC, which feed into PKA and then Akt (pakts473). Akt is not known to act back on plcg. So A, plcg causes pakts473, is more likely than B, even if the effect is indirect.
